data.review_body:
I recently made a purchase through Aliexpress, as I always do, but unfortunately this time the products arrived completely damaged and unusable due to poor packaging by the seller.
When I contacted Aliexpress to resolve the problem, they only refunded me 10% of the amount paid, meaning I lost my money.
In short, I trusted Aliexpress and this time I was left without money and without the product.
Avoid buying from Aliexpress; if something goes wrong, they will go against the buyer, always protecting dishonest sellers.
To make matters worse, I requested the cancellation and closure of my Aliexpress account, which was denied.
I am here now to report my case so that the same thing does not happen to other people.
I also want to emphasize to Aliexpress that for 50 SEK, you lost a customer who spent much more than that per month.
Aliexpress, please cancel my account and delete it!
data.review_headline: They refuse to delete and remove my account.

data.review_body:
I ordered a dress to be made from a company called Fatapaese. I said all along for the dress to be made out of crepe. I said this right from the beginning the dress was to be Crepe and beaded lace. 
I got imitation silk and plain lace.
Not once was imitation silk even mentioned. 
The first dress they lied to me about it saying it had been made and shipped. That was a lie. They admitted they should have told me the truth.
So I sent the specifications of the picture which always said crepe and beaded lace. 
There were no live videos and photos of the making of the dress.
They showed me a picture right at the end and I had no idea it was not crepe and beaded lace.
I have the whole transcript from beginning to end. I only ever mentioned crepe and beaded lace. The picture was shown and shipped at the same time. I said to them I only want the dress if it's in crepe and beaded lace. They led me to believe this was what I was getting. Not once did imitation silk get mentioned. 
It was only when I received the dress I knew the material was incorrect.
So I opened a dispute saying item not as ordered.
Ali Express did not care. Although I provided all the transcript that said a crepe dress and beaded lace they did not care and ruled in favour of the seller.
$277 it cost me for a dress I did not order in the material they made it in.
PayPal did not want to know either because they don't cover customised dresses. Although the item was not as described. 
Don't trust the sellers or Ali Express. They do as they please and there is no protection for the buyer. 
This was a dress for my daughter's wedding.
I had already had 2 other dresses made by another company that were the wrong size and they got away with that too. They were Charmant Wedding Stire Don't trust them. They can make inferior products and get away with it.i paid over $600 for nothing. I cannot wear any of the dresses because they were made incorrectly. Ali Express say this is ok.
Pay more and go local.

The seller is just rude! And he’s sympathizing with my bad experience! I haven’t encountered anything like this in a long time. You only see this with inexperienced sellers or scammers!
How much information can be transmitted?  Two months of negotiations, AliExpress played the role of a benefactor, but the seller did not sell the product, but pushed it (he applied a vague and concrete description of the product, but an expanded one, and after the order and payment, the initial description of the product changed to another, as in a fairy tale!).  It's not decent!
When returning the goods from Lithuania, the Chinese customs stopped the Chinese returned goods without explanation. AliExpress does nothing to release and refund the money for the goods. So AliExpress feeds the goods to the Chinese customs, probably they do not have enough salary!
Such cheap and two-faced people simply need to be avoided! The laws here are only in concepts, not in action.

I purchased a hair brush through AliExpress and unfortunately received a defective product.

I understand that manufacturing defects can happen with any company. My disappointment is not with the defect itself, but with how AliExpress handles these situations.

The only solutions offered were:

accept a small partial refund and keep a defective product; or
package the item myself, travel to a post office, and complete the entire return process in order to receive a full refund.

The issue is not the product's value (around US$10). The issue is the principle.

As a good-faith customer, I fulfilled my part of the contract: I selected the product, paid for it, and waited for delivery. The defective product was entirely the seller's responsibility. Nevertheless, AliExpress transferred the burden of solving the problem to me, requiring me to spend my own time and effort on a return process that I never agreed to when I made the purchase.

When everything goes well, delivery is made to my home. When something goes wrong because of the supplier, I'm expected to become part of their reverse logistics operation.

I find this policy unfair and contrary to what good customer service should look like. I expected AliExpress to take responsibility for resolving a problem it caused, instead of transferring the inconvenience to the customer.

I hope the company reviews this policy and adopts a more customer-friendly approach in cases where defective products are delivered.
data.review_headline: Poor after-sales support when a defective product is delivered

data.review_body: WORST refund process.  I bought 2 identical pairs of shoes, just in different sizes.  Neither fit and had to be returned.  Even though both pairs arrived to me TOGETHER, AliExpress made me return them separately (even though I began the return process at the same time).  I chatted with AA to express my concerns that separating the two pairs of shoes might cause return delivery issues, especially since AA had me return one pair via Fed Ex and the other pair via USPS.  My concerns turned out to be valid.  One return pair of shoes was received by AA and they refunded me.  However, AA claimed they did not receive the other pair.  Like I said, they should not have been returned separately since I received them together originally.  I had ample documentation from USPS stating that the items was delivered to the Linwood, NJ post office AND that the item was actually picked up by an individual.  As directed by AA, I even had my USPS receipt stamped with the USPS official seal and signed by USPS staff.  I had at least 3 disputes over this and at least 3 trips to USPS.  I sent AA reasonable proof that the item was in fact returned to the post office AND picked up by an individual.  It was not good enough for AA to refund me a crummy $11.82!  The would NOT have happened if AA permitted me to return both pairs together, just like they were delivered to me originally.  I have had to return many things over the years to Temu, Shein, Walmart, Amazon, Etsy, and Ebay and I have never dealt with such impossible requests.  Although the AliExpress chat teams have been professional and empathetic, I felt like they "yessssed" me to death, but did nothing.  I deactivated my AliExpress account and will NEVER do business with AA again.

data.review_body:
AliExpress publicly asked me to update my email because they cannot reach me. Their own mail server has been rejecting all connections for weeks. I have the bounce logs. They cannot reach me because of them. They are asking me to fix it

This is not a communication failure on my end. I have submitted my contact information and responded to every request through the "Request Information" form more than 40 times over the course of this case. Each time, I receive an identical automated message claiming my email could not be confirmed, followed by another request to resubmit the same information.

This is not a technical issue. It is a pattern designed to generate the appearance of non-response while the protection window runs out. I have screenshots and timestamps of every submission, and this correspondence is being added to the case file already submitted to my bank as part of the chargeback proceeding.

I am not resubmitting my contact information a 41st time. My email is on file and has been on file since my first submission. If AliExpress is unable to locate it, that is an internal system failure, not a failure of communication on my part.
data.review_headline: THEY BLAMED MY EMAIL. THEIR SERVER CAUSED IT
